title: EKS Control Plane Audit

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.64 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.64 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatchlogs` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatchlogs" log_group="/aws/eks/*/cluster"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.64_eks_control_plane_audit_64"
| sort -_time
description: Kubernetes audit logs capture who changed roles, secrets, and workloads; essential for forensics and SOC2 evidence on EKS.
value: Detecting eks control plane audit early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable EKS audit logging to CloudWatch Logs and subscribe to Splunk. Optionally include CloudTrail for `CreateCluster`, `AssociateIdentityProviderConfig`. Alert on cluster-admin bindings, anonymous access, or secret reads from unexpected service accounts.
visualization: Table (user, resource, count), Timeline (privileged API calls), Sankey (user→namespace).
cimSpl: | tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Change.All_Changes by All_Changes.user | sort - count
dataModelAcceleration: Change (All_Changes): for CloudTrail management events mapped to CIM. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Platform or GitOps that edits `clusterroles` or `secrets` during a cluster upgrade; compare with the release runbook.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatchlogs`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable EKS audit logging to CloudWatch Logs and subscribe to Splunk. Optionally include CloudTrail for `CreateCluster`, `AssociateIdentityProviderConfig`. Alert on cluster-admin bindings, anonymous access, or secret reads from unexpected service accounts.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatchlogs" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatchlogs" log_group="/aws/eks/*/cluster"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.64_eks_control_plane_audit_64"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatchlogs` in `index=aws` to detect eks control plane audit. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_64_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (user, resource, count), Timeline (privileged API calls), Sankey (user→namespace)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of eks control plane audit so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
